title: Rhombus_Botnet_Investigation_eb2
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a suspected Rhombus botnet infection on a Linux-based network. The botnet is known to target VPS and IoT devices, acting as a dropper for additional malware and engaging in DDoS activities. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the botnet activity.
outcomes: Identify unauthorized or suspicious services responsible for periodic external communication.
Distinguish malicious traffic generation services from legitimate network services.
Identify persistence mechanisms used by the botnet.
Analyze network traffic to identify ports used by botnet communication.
Determine the target of the flooding activity.
Collect forensic evidence supporting the identified botnet activity.
Correlate collected evidence to classify the observed behavior as botnet activity or legitimate system behavior.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a suspected Rhombus botnet infection on a Linux-based network. The botnet is known to target VPS and IoT devices, acting as a dropper for additional malware and engaging in DDoS activities. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the botnet activity.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox via the provided cloud environment. Use the following credentials to log in via SSH: `username: cyrano`, `password: cyrano`. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Access the local sandbox via SSH using the following credentials: `username: cyrano`, `password: cyrano`. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Suspicious Beacon Service Discovery
levels.content: Investigate the host `bot1` and identify an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication. This service is likely associated with botnet activity.
levels.solution:
To identify the suspicious service, you can use the following commands:

1. List all running services:
   ```bash
   systemctl list-units --type=service
   ```

2. Look for any unusual or recently created services, particularly those named `bot-beacon-RHOMBUS`.

3. Check the service details:
   ```bash
   systemctl status bot-beacon-RHOMBUS.service
   ```

The service name is `bot-beacon-RHOMBUS.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with names that include 'bot' or 'beacon'.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service name starts with 'bot-' and includes 'beacon'. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

levels.title: Suspicious Flood Service Discovery
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic on `bot1`. This service is likely part of the botnet's DDoS capabilities.
levels.solution:
To identify the suspicious flood service, you can use the following commands:

1. List all running services:
   ```bash
   systemctl list-units --type=service
   ```

2. Look for any unusual or recently created services, particularly those named `bot-flood-RHOMBUS`.

3. Check the service details:
   ```bash
   systemctl status bot-flood-RHOMBUS.service
   ```

The service name is `bot-flood-RHOMBUS.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd services and network connections for any suspicious activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with names that include 'flood' or 'bot'.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service name starts with 'bot-' and includes 'flood'. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious services identified in the previous tasks are automatically started after reboot on `bot1`.
levels.solution:
To identify the persistence mechanisms, you can use the following commands:

1. List all systemd timers:
   ```bash
   systemctl list-timers
   ```

2. Look for any unusual or recently created timers, particularly those named `bot-beacon-RHOMBUS.timer` or `bot-flood-RHOMBUS.timer`.

3. Check the timer details:
   ```bash
   systemctl status bot-beacon-RHOMBUS.timer
   systemctl status bot-flood-RHOMBUS.timer
   ```

The persistence mechanisms are `bot-beacon-RHOMBUS.timer` and `bot-flood-RHOMBUS.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the systemd timers and services for any persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with names that include 'bot' or 'beacon'.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The timer name starts with 'bot-' and includes 'beacon'. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.
